newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche metals/oil index points higher in '97/98.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche metals/oil index points higher in '97/98.

text.p: Prices of industrial raw materials and crude oil are forecast to rise by eight percent in the second half of 1997 and by two percent in 1998, Deutsche Bank Research said on publication of a new monthly price index.
"...these forecasts are consistent with an expected increase in inflation in the G-7 countries to about 2.5 percent in 1997 and almost three percent in 1998," DBR said on Friday.
The DBR-CI index represents six base and three precious metals which together account for 27.6 percent of the total, while crude oil accounts for 72.4 percent.
It excludes agricultural commodities, which makes it less complex than other indices, but DBR says it creates a stronger link between raw materials prices and inflation.
DBR-CI prices fell by 18 percent on average in first half 1997 when sharp oil price falls offset a 9.3 percent increase in base metals prices.
DBR analyst Peter Cornelius said Iraq's return to the oil market was negative for prices but this would be outweighed by strong demand.
Brent crude, which broke above $19 this week, may stabilise around $18.50-18.75 per barrel in the second half, according to DBR.
Cornelius also saw favourable medium-term prospects for base metals prices, due to fundamentals, technical squeezes and speculative interest.

He said aluminium and copper prices held most promise, while zinc was also recovering and lead could benefit from the onset of the battery season, the winter period when demand for car batteries is at its highest.
Weights in the index have been derived from import values of the specific commodities in industrialised countries, with 1990 as the base year, and are detailed as follows --
Crude oil 72.4 percent, metals 27.6 percent, of which aluminium 6.4, copper 6.2, gold 5.8, lead 0.5, nickel 2.3, platinum 1.4, silver 2.8, tin 0.7, zinc 1.5.
